items.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: my brother, among other records he collected, he loved Lunceford and Goodman and Basie especially

ctx.x: Tracing the lineage from that, from that trumpet player to another all-time favorite of mine, tell us what you know about Dizzy.

Well Dizzy I always say was one-half of my heartbeat and Charlie Parker was the other, but there are a lot of other people too, Lester Young especially and Coleman Hawkins, people like that. And many, many others. But I discovered Dizzy and Charlie Parker when I was in high school and I had already been listening to jazz for a long time, but they hit me like a revelation. I became really a fanatic about them. I tried to convert everyone I met, “You’ve got to listen to this.” And I’ve told this story a number of…

a week in the course of his program he would go to a live wire from some club. And this was a club on 52nd Street. In going back and doing some research, I learned it was The Onyx, and there was Dizzy and Oscar Pettiford and that, what is called the first bebop band to play, you know, as a cohesive unit, with heads that were very typical of the music as it was developing at that time. And I heard this guy playing the trumpet who was announced as Dizzy Gillespie, and I said it sounds like he’s playing some wrong…
